spans.s: (I)--a King of extensive learning, had a friend whose name and behaviour were not known; went in search of a suitable place for the realisation of various pleasures; this he found in a city of nine entrances resembling [page२-345+ ३८] भोगवती on the southern side of the हिमालयस्. By accident he met a charming lady protected by a serpent and followed by a number of ladies and men; moved by her charms he requested her to be his wife and she agreed; For a hundred years they continued to enjoy pleasures; पुरञ्जन used to visit the kingdoms, विभ्राजित, Saurabha, दक्षिण and Uttara पाञ्चालस्, ग्रामक, वैशस and others through the different entrances of the city guarded by the Superintendent; influenced by her charms he came com- pletely under her control; mad with desire for hunting, once he left his queen and went to the forest and after killing many a game, he returned home and desired to meet the queen whom he found lying on the bare ground in misery; he consoled her and once more yielded to her love and influence at the cost of his youth; he had

(I)--alias इन्द्रवाह; also Kakustha: son of विकुक्षि father of Anenas; in a देवासुर war he became पार्ष्णिग्राह to the Devas when Indra assumed the form of a bull over which he rode and discomfited the Asuras by his भल्ल weapons; hence known as Kakustha; a राजऋषि. भा.

(III)--the last of the बार्हद्रथ line; was killed by his minister शुनक who placed his own son on the throne. भा.

years; got back his youth and was anointed king; progenitor of the Paurava वम्श; father of Janame- jaya; in his line were Brahmanas, क्षत्रियस् and the Bha- ratas; blessed by ययाती to have good sons; a legal point was raised by the members of the Assembly as to the legality of his succession to the throne when there was the eldest, Yadu, the grandson of शुक्र; ययाति explained that mere birth was no qualification for it was character that counted; the conduct of the eldest son was unsatisfactory and hence the youngest was chosen; this was approved by the Paura- [page२-375+ ३०] जानपदस्;
